title: Rollout Thermometer Ledger — personal calibration notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal ledger for a metric-driven canary ramp I want to iterate on. Not a final runbook — more of a sensorboard: what I check, the order, and the fast signals I act on. Keep language terse; this lives as an experimental crib to bring to post-mortems.

TL;DR: create a small ‘thermometer’ score (0–100) that aggregates safety/quality signals. Only move the percent slider when thermometer >= threshold for 15m. Stop and hold when any major signal flips. Use a backing time-series window and explicit degradation counters to avoid noisy flip-flops.

Thermometer composition (weights are intentionally conservative):
- Latency stability (p95 vs baseline): weight 30. Window: 10m rolling. Score contribution: 100 if p95 change < +20ms, linearly down to 0 at +200ms.
- Error surface: weight 30. Error = user-facing 5xx + model-eval-failures + malformed responses. 100 if error rate < 0.05% over window, 0 at 1%.
- Quality regressions (offline eval): weight 20. Use daily eval harness on the canary prompt set. 100 if relative quality >= 99% of baseline; 0 at <= 95%.
- Cost delta / token anomalies: weight 10. 100 if cost per 1k tokens within +/-5% baseline; 0 at +30% or anomaly detected.
- Observability health: weight 10. 100 if tracing/metrics are present and ingestion delay < 30s; 0 if metric gaps or ingestion > 2m.

Thermometer thresholds => rollout policy (example):
- Thermometer < 35: hold, rollback candidate if previously moved.
- Thermometer 35–59: safe to unfreeze only for diagnostics (no population increase).
- Thermometer 60–74: allow +1% traffic increment every 20m (max 5%/hour).
- Thermometer 75–89: allow +5% every 30m (max 15%/hour).
- Thermometer >= 90: accelerate to production rate (hand-off to autoscale rules).

Gating rules (hard stops):
- Absolute: p95 > baseline + 250ms OR errors increase by factor > 3x over 5m -> immediate rollback to last stable pinned version.
- Relative: >0.5% user-facing correctness regressions on sampled production prompts -> pause and open incident channel.
- Observability: if logs/traces drop out for >90s, hold.

Warmup sequencing (cohorts):
1) Shadow: 0% traffic, full logging & trace. Run for 30m min.
2) Micro-cohort (internal-only): 0.5% traffic, chosen by user-agent tag (internal clients). 30m watch.
3) External pilot: 3% traffic across 3 regions (balanced). 60m watch.
4) Gradual ramp per thermometer rules.

Pinning notes (practical commands and reminders):
- When pinning a model for an account: record commit + model-id in the ledger and create a short-lived tag in the control plane. e.g.,
  rwdctl model pin --model-id rgx-3.4.1 --tenant acme-corp --expires 2026-03-15
- Use descriptive reason: "pin: post-canary freeze due to latency drift investigation". This helps later audits.
- If rolling forward: create a canary diff snapshot (metrics + debug logs) and attach to the rollout ticket before unpin.

Quick checklist before each increment (10–15s mental checklist):
- telemetry OK (p95, errors, traces) for last 15m?
- sample sanity check (5 curated prompts) run in sandbox?
- infra capacity headroom >= 20% in target region?
- linked customer pins? any account pinned to previous version?
- open incidents or maintenance windows in calendar?

Fast signals I actually act on during nights/weekends (because we want very low cognitive load):
- one-off high-severity error spikes (SLO breach) -> immediate rollback.
- sustained latency degradation (>3x / sustained 10m) -> pause ramp, notify SRE.
- data quality anomaly flagged by eval harness -> pause, snapshot and alert ML team.

Telemetry instrumentation checklist (what I look for first in Grafana):
- p50/p95/p99 median baselines (per-region)
- error_budget_consumption and request_failure_rate
- rollout_thermometer_score (composed) with component breakdown series
- sample_responses: random sample pipeline for semantic checks
- cost_per_1k_tokens and token_count_deltas

Runbook snippet (quick actions):
- To pause: rwdctl rollout set --id <rollout-id> --state PAUSED --note "thermometer: <reason>"
- To rollback: rwdctl rollout revert --id <rollout-id> --to-version <last-stable-version> --force --note "auto-rollback: <signal>"
- To audit pin history: rwdctl model pins list --tenant <id> --since 2025-01-01

Retrospective capture fields (what I scribble after a run):
- time windows and thermometer trace (attach PNG)
- prime failing component (latency / errors / quality / telemetry)
- what we changed in model or infra that might explain the delta
- screencap of the 5 failing prompt samples (if any)
- action items and owner

Open questions / stuff to test next week:
- Does 10m rolling window create too many oscillations for bursty traffic patterns? Try 30m window on canary-only cohorts.
- How often do offline evals disagree with live sampling? Add a daily reconciliation job that surfaces mismatches > 1%
- Could we use a Bayesian smoothing on thermometer instead of linear thresholds? Simulate with historical canaries.

Notes-to-self: keep the thermometer interpretable. If ML or infra people can't explain a drop within 10m, we should default to HLD (hold) and escalate. The goal is to reduce heroics during peaks and make the first action always the same: collect snapshot, notify owner, and hold.

Small mental model: thermometer is an ensemble of safety sensors, not a detector. It helps pace increases and surfaces which sensor tripped. The name must remind me to check components, not just an aggregate number.

Last bits: when experimenting, log the exact rollout-id and snapshot-id in the ticket and pin a short slack note to #releases with the thermometer link. Keep the cadence conservative for accounts with strict SLAs (>= 99.9% availability).

-- Omar

(End of ledger entry)
